metadata.title: Whittaker vectors in singular Whittaker modules

extraction_notes.note: claim or definition: the sentence asserts irreducibility over the derived subalgebra and also introduces $\mathfrak{s}=[\mathfrak{l},\mathfrak{l}]$; kept as one claim node since the sentence cannot be split.
Step rule 8 treats 'Conversely' as a case marker; here it opens the other direction of an iff, so the two directions are marked case_split steps.

The base-case sentence is immediate ('trivial') under step rule 6 and was appended to the WLOG setup sentence; the merged step is typed induction_step so the induction still has two induction_step steps (PSP15, PSP18).
Introduction restatements of the main theorem, corollary and the Whittaker-module definitions, and the sentence before Corollary 3.3 restating it, are repeated statements and get no node.

nodes.name: Semisimple Lie algebra setup
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra ${\mathfrak h}$, root system $\Phi$, base $\Delta$ of simple roots, and corresponding set $\Phi_+$ of positive roots.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a complex semisimple Lie algebra g with Cartan subalgebra h, roots Phi, simple roots Delta and positive roots Phi_+.

nodes.name: Nilradical of the standard Borel
nodes.statement: Let $\mathfrak{g}$, ${\mathfrak h}$, $\Phi$, $\Phi_+$, and $\Delta$ be as in Section 1, and let $\mathfrak{n}$ be the nilradical of the standard Borel $\mathfrak{b}$ relative to $(\mathfrak{g},{\mathfrak h},\Delta)$.

nodes.name: Whittaker character
nodes.statement: A Lie algebra homomorphism $\psi:\ \mathfrak{n}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is called a {\em Whittaker character}; the character $\psi$ is {\em non-singular} if it is nonzero on the root spaces $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$ for all simple roots $\alpha\in\Delta$.
nodes.statement_short: A Whittaker character is a Lie algebra homomorphism psi: n -> C; it is non-singular if nonzero on every simple root space.

nodes.name: Whittaker vector
nodes.statement: An element $v$ of a $\mathfrak{g}$-module $V$ is said to be a {\em Whittaker vector of type} $\psi$ if $xv=\psi(x)v$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$.

nodes.name: Space of Whittaker vectors Wh V
nodes.statement: The space of Whittaker vectors in $V$ will be denoted by $\hbox{Wh}\,V$.

nodes.name: Whittaker module
nodes.statement: Cyclic modules generated by Whittaker vectors of type $\psi$ are called {\em Whittaker modules of type} $\psi$ and are {\em singular} or {\em non-singular}, depending on whether $\psi$ is singular or non-singular.
differentia: generated by Whittaker vectors of type $\psi$

nodes.name: Uniqueness of the Whittaker character
nodes.statement: Each Whittaker module admits a unique Whittaker character, so the notions of singular and non-singular are well defined.
conclusions: Each Whittaker module admits a unique Whittaker character

nodes.name: Support Delta_psi of a Whittaker character
nodes.statement: Let $\psi$ be a Whittaker character, and let $\Delta_\psi$ be the set of simple roots $\alpha$ for which $\psi(\mathfrak{g}_\alpha)\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Levi subalgebra l_psi
nodes.statement: We write $\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_\psi$ for the reductive subalgebra generated by the sum of ${\mathfrak h}$ and the root spaces $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$ with $\pm\alpha\in \Delta_\psi$.

nodes.name: Triangular decomposition of l
nodes.statement: The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{l}$ has a triangular decomposition $\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_-\oplus{\mathfrak h}\oplus\mathfrak{l}_+$, where $\mathfrak{l}_+$ and $\mathfrak{l}_-$ are the intersections of $\mathfrak{l}$ with the positive and negative root spaces of $\mathfrak{g}$, respectively.

nodes.name: Parabolic subalgebra p
nodes.statement: The centre $\mathfrak{z}$ of $\mathfrak{l}$ lies in ${\mathfrak h}$, and the corresponding parabolic subalgebra $\mathfrak{l}+\mathfrak{n}$ will be denoted by $\mathfrak{p}$.

nodes.name: Decomposition p = l + m
nodes.statement: The subalgebra $\mathfrak{p}$ has a unique $\operatorname{ad}{\mathfrak h}$-stable decomposition $\mathfrak{p}=\mathfrak{l}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, and $\mathfrak{g}=\overline{\mathfrak{m}}\oplus\mathfrak{l}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, where $\overline{\mathfrak{m}}$ is the Lie subalgebra spanned by the root spaces $\mathfrak{g}_{-\alpha}$ for which $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$ is contained in $\mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: p splits ad h-stably as l + m, and g = m-bar + l + m with m-bar spanned by the opposite root spaces.

nodes.name: Centre of the enveloping algebra
nodes.statement: For any Lie algebra $\mathfrak{a}$, let  $Z(\mathfrak{a})$ be the centre of its enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak{a})$.

nodes.name: Induced l-module Y_{Omega,psi}
nodes.statement:
For an arbitrary central character $\Omega:\,Z(\mathfrak{l})\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$, consider the induced $\mathfrak{l}$-module
$$Y_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{l})\otimes_{Z(\mathfrak{l})U(\mathfrak{l}_+)}\mathbb{C}v_{\Omega,\psi},$$
where $Z(\mathfrak{l})U(\mathfrak{l}_+)=Z(\mathfrak{l})\otimes U(\mathfrak{l}_+)$ acts by the characters $\Omega$ and $\psi$ on the $1$-dimensional space spanned by the vector $v_{\Omega,\psi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Y_{Omega,psi} is the l-module induced from the 1-dimensional Z(l)U(l_+)-module on which Z(l) acts by Omega and l_+ by psi.

nodes.name: Simplicity of Y_{Omega,psi}
nodes.statement: As the Whittaker character $\psi$ is nonzero on each root space $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Delta_\psi$, it is easy to show that $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ is a simple left $U(\mathfrak{l})$-module.
assumptions: the Whittaker character $\psi$ is nonzero on each root space $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$ with $\alpha\in\Delta_\psi$

nodes.name: Y_{Omega,psi} remains simple over the derived subalgebra
nodes.statement: It remains irreducible when restricted to the (semisimple) derived subalgebra $\mathfrak{s}=[\mathfrak{l},\mathfrak{l}]$ of $\mathfrak{l}$.
conclusions: It remains irreducible when restricted to the (semisimple) derived subalgebra $\mathfrak{s}=[\mathfrak{l},\mathfrak{l}]$ of $\mathfrak{l}$

nodes.name: Induced Whittaker module M_{Omega,psi}
nodes.statement:
We regard $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ as a left $U(\mathfrak{p})$-module via the inflation map $\mathfrak{p}\rightarrow\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{l}$.  Inducing to $U(\mathfrak{g})$ gives the Whittaker module
$$M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Inflate Y_{Omega,psi} to p and induce to g to get the Whittaker module M_{Omega,psi}.

nodes.name: McDowell's classification of simple Whittaker modules
nodes.statement: {\em \cite[Theorem 2.9]{mcdowell85}} The module $M_{\Omega,\psi}$ has a unique simple quotient $L_{\Omega,\psi}$, and every simple Whittaker module of type $\psi$ is isomorphic to a module $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ for some character $\Omega:\ Z(\mathfrak{l})\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$.\hfill $\Box$
conclusions: The module $M_{\Omega,\psi}$ has a unique simple quotient $L_{\Omega,\psi}$
every simple Whittaker module of type $\psi$ is isomorphic to a module $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ for some character $\Omega:\ Z(\mathfrak{l})\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$
nodes.statement_short: M_{Omega,psi} has a unique simple quotient L_{Omega,psi}, and these exhaust the simple Whittaker modules of type psi.

nodes.name: Partial order on z^*
nodes.statement: Define a partial order $\preceq$ on its algebraic dual $\mathfrak{z}^*$ by setting $\eta\preceq\mu$ if $\mu-\eta$ is the restriction of an element $\lambda\in\hbox{Span}_{\mathbb{Z}_+}(\Delta\setminus\Delta_\psi)$ to $\mathfrak{z}$.
nodes.statement_short: eta precedes mu when mu - eta restricts from a nonnegative integer combination of simple roots outside Delta_psi.

nodes.name: Simplicity criterion for Whittaker modules
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a Whittaker module for $\mathfrak{g}$. Then $V$ is simple if and only if $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional.
assumptions: Let $V$ be a Whittaker module for $\mathfrak{g}$.
conclusions: $V$ is simple if and only if $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional.
nodes.label: mainthm

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi:\ \etaightarrow\mathbb{C}$ be the Whittaker character of $V$. The module $V$ has an obvious filtration $V= igcup_{k=0}^\infty V^{(k)}$, where $$V^{(k)}=\{v\in V:\ x_0 ullet x_1 ullet\cdots ullet x_k ullet v=0\hbox{\ for all\ }x_0,x_1,\ldots ,x_k\in\mathfrak{n}\},$$ and $x ullet v$ is defined as $xv-\psi(x)v$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$ and $v\in V$. Let $v$ be a nonzero element of $V$. If $v
otin\hbox{Wh}\,V$, then $x ullet v
eq0$ for some $x\in\mathfrak{n}$. But $x ullet v\in V^{(k-1)}$ whenever $v\in V^{(k)}$, so $V^{(0)}\cap U(\mathfrak{g})v
eq 0$. If $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional and spanned by a vector $w$, then by definition, $V^{(0)}=\hbox{Wh}\,V=\mathbb{C}w$ and $V=U(\mathfrak{g})w$. In this case, we see that $\mathbb{C}w= V^{(0)}\subseteq U(\mathfrak{g})v$. Since $w$ generates $V$, the module $V$ is thus simple when $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional. Conversely, by McDowell's classification, any simple Whittaker module is of the form $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ for some Whittaker character $\psi:\ \mathfrak{n}ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ and central character $\Omega\in Z(\mathfrak{l}_\psi)^*$. The centre $\mathfrak{z}$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_\psi$ acts semisimply on $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$. Since $\mathfrak{z}\subseteq\mathfrak{h}$, it also acts semisimply on the induced module $M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ and on its simple quotient $L_{\Omega,\psi}$. That is, $$M_{\Omega,\psi}= igoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak{z}^*}M_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\hbox{\ and\ }L_{\Omega,\psi}= igoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak{z}^*}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu,$$ where $V^\mu=\{v\in V\ :\ hv=\mu(h)v\hbox{\ for all\ }h\in\mathfrak{z}\}$ for any $\mathfrak{g}$-module $V$. Since $\mathfrak{z}$ acts on $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ by the restriction $\overline{\Omega}$ of the character $\Omega$ to $\mathfrak{z}$, it acts on $$M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}})\otimes_\mathbb{C}U(\mathfrak{p})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}})\otimes_\mathbb{C} Y_{\Omega,\psi}$$ by weights bounded above by $\overline{\Omega}$. Similarly,  egin{equation} L_{\Omega,\psi}= igoplus_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu. \end{equation} Let $v$ be a Whittaker vector in $L_{\Omega,\psi}$, with decomposition $v=\sum_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}v_\mu$ relative to (ef{star}). Let $x\in\mathfrak{n}=\mathfrak{l}_+\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ be a root vector in a root space $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$. If $x\in\mathfrak{l}_+$, then $\mathfrak{z}$ commutes with $x$ and $xL_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\subseteq L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu$. In particular, $\sum_\mu\psi(x)v_\mu=xv=\sum_\mu xv_\mu$, so by comparing graded components, $xv_\mu=\psi(x)v_\mu$ for all $\mu$. If $x\in\mathfrak{m}$, then $$zx=x(z+\alpha(z)),$$ for all $z\in\mathfrak{z}$, so $$xL_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\subseteq L_{\Omega,\psi}^{\mu+\overline{\alpha}},$$ where $\overline{\alpha}$ is the restriction of $\alpha$ to $\mathfrak{z}$. But $\psi$ vanishes on $\mathfrak{m}$ by construction, so $$0=xv=\sum_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}xv_\mu.$$ Each $xv_\mu$ belongs to a distinct graded component, so $xv_\mu=0$ for all $\mu$. The subalgebras $\mathfrak{l}_+$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ are spanned by root vectors, so $xv_\mu=\psi(x)v_\mu$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$ and $\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}$. That is, $v_\mu\in\hbox{Wh}\,V$ for all $\mu$. Let $\mu\prec\overline{\Omega}$. Then by degree considerations, the submodule $$U(\mathfrak{g})v_\mu=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}}\oplus\mathfrak{l})v_\mu\subseteq\sum_{\lambda\preceq\mu}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\lambda$$ is proper in $L_{\Omega,\psi}$. As $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ is simple, we see that $v_\mu=0$ and $v=v_{\overline{\Omega}}$. Therefore, $v$ is a Whittaker vector in the simple $\mathfrak{s}$-Whittaker module $Y_{\Omega,\psi}=L_{\Omega,\psi}^{\overline{\Omega}}$ of type $\overline{\psi}$, where $\overline{\psi}$ is the restriction of $\psi$ to the positive part $\mathfrak{l}_+$ of $\mathfrak{s}=[\mathfrak{l},\mathfrak{l}]$. As $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ is non-singular, Kostant's criterion \cite[Theorem 3.6.1]{kostant78} applies, and its space $W$ of Whittaker vectors is $1$-dimensional. The space $\hbox{Wh}\,L_{\Omega,\psi}\subseteq W$ is thus also $1$-dimensional.\hfill $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Filtration argument for simplicity when Wh V is 1-dimensional; conversely, decompose L_{Omega,psi} into z-weight spaces and show each Whittaker vector lies in the top component Y_{Omega,psi}. Key step: reduction to Kostant's non-singular criterion for Y_{Omega,psi}.

nodes.name: z-weight decomposition of L_{Omega,psi}
nodes.statement: L_{\Omega,\psi}=\bigoplus_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu.
nodes.label: star

nodes.name: Category N of locally n-finite modules
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be the category of $\mathfrak{g}$-modules which are locally finite with respect to the action of $\mathfrak{n}$.
differentia: locally finite with respect to the action of $\mathfrak{n}$

nodes.name: Whittaker vectors bounded by composition length
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak{g}$-module in the category $\mathcal{N}$. Then $\dim\hbox{Wh}\,M$ is bounded by the length of $M$.
assumptions: Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak{g}$-module in the category $\mathcal{N}$.
conclusions: $\dim\hbox{Wh}\,M$ is bounded by the length of $M$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.3
nodes.statement: Without loss of generality, we may assume that $M$ is of finite length and has a composition series $$0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_\ell=M.$$ We induct on the length $\ell$ of $M$, and as the base case $\ell=0$ is trivial, we may assume that $\ell>0$. For any $i>0$ and nonzero $m\in M_i/M_{i-1}$, the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{n}$ acts on the finite dimensional space $U(\mathfrak{n})m$. By Lie's theorem, $U(\mathfrak{n})m\subseteq M_i/M_{i-1}$ contains a nonzero Whittaker vector $n$, and by simplicity $M_i/M_{i-1}=U(\mathfrak{g})n$ is thus a Whittaker module. The space $\hbox{Wh}(M_i/M_{i-1})$ is $1$-dimensional by Theorem \ref{mainthm}. If $v,w\in M$ are nonzero Whittaker vectors, then their images $v+M_{\ell-1}$ and $w+M_{\ell-1}$ lie in the $1$-dimensional space $\hbox{Wh}(M_\ell/M_{\ell-1})$. The vector $v$ is thus of the form $\lambda w + u$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $u\in M_{\ell-1}$. As $u=v-\lambda w$ is clearly also a Whittaker vector and $\dim\hbox{Wh}(M_{\ell-1})\leq \ell-1$ by induction, it follows that $\dim\hbox{Wh}\,M\leq 1+\dim\hbox{Wh}(M_{\ell-1})\leq\ell.$\hfill $\Box$
nodes.statement_short: Induction on composition length: each simple subquotient is a Whittaker module (Lie's theorem) with 1-dimensional Wh by Theorem 3.2.

nodes.name: Universal Whittaker modules with central character
nodes.statement: {\em Any Whittaker module $V$ of type $\psi$ that admits a central character $\chi:\ Z(\mathfrak{g})\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is a quotient of a universal module $$\mathcal{Y}_{\chi,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g})\otimes_{Z(\mathfrak{g})U(\mathfrak{n})}\mathbb{C}w_{\chi,\psi},$$ where $Z(\mathfrak{g})U(\mathfrak{n})=Z(\mathfrak{g})\otimes U(\mathfrak{n})$ acts on the $1$-dimensional space $\mathbb{C}w_{\chi,\psi}$ by $\chi\otimes\psi$. Such modules are always simple if $\psi$ is non-singular, but need not be simple for singular $\psi$. By the above corollary, the dimension of $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is bounded by the length of $\mathcal{Y}_{\chi,\psi}$. Such lengths have been computed by Mili\v{c}i\'c and Soergel \cite{milicic-soergel97} using Kazhdan-Lusztig theory. }
nodes.statement_short: Whittaker modules with central character chi are quotients of a universal module Y_{chi,psi}, whose length bounds dim Wh V (lengths known by Milicic-Soergel).

nodes.name: Whittaker filtration
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi:\ \eta\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ be the Whittaker character of $V$.  The module $V$ has an obvious filtration $V=\bigcup_{k=0}^\infty V^{(k)}$, where
  $$V^{(k)}=\{v\in V:\ x_0\bullet x_1\bullet\cdots\bullet x_k\bullet v=0\hbox{\ for all\ }x_0,x_1,\ldots ,x_k\in\mathfrak{n}\},$$
  and $x\bullet v$ is defined as $xv-\psi(x)v$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$ and $v\in V$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the filtration V^(k) by iterated twisted action of n.

nodes.name: Every cyclic submodule meets V^(0)
nodes.statement:
Let $v$ be a nonzero element of $V$.  If $v
otin\hbox{Wh}\,V$, then $x ullet v
eq0$ for some $x\in\mathfrak{n}$.  But $x ullet v\in V^{(k-1)}$ whenever $v\in V^{(k)}$, so $V^{(0)}\cap U(\mathfrak{g})v
eq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Show every nonzero cyclic submodule meets V^(0).

nodes.name: Case Wh V one-dimensional
nodes.statement: If $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional and spanned by a vector $w$, then by definition, $V^{(0)}=\hbox{Wh}\,V=\mathbb{C}w$ and $V=U(\mathfrak{g})w$.  In this case, we see that $\mathbb{C}w= V^{(0)}\subseteq U(\mathfrak{g})v$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume Wh V = Cw; then w lies in every cyclic submodule.

nodes.name: V is simple
nodes.statement: Since $w$ generates $V$, the module $V$ is thus simple when $\hbox{Wh}\,V$ is $1$-dimensional.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude V is simple when Wh V is 1-dimensional.

nodes.name: Converse via McDowell's classification
nodes.statement: Conversely, by McDowell's classification, any simple Whittaker module is of the form $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ for some Whittaker character $\psi:\ \mathfrak{n}\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$ and central character $\Omega\in Z(\mathfrak{l}_\psi)^*$.
nodes.statement_short: For the converse, reduce to L_{Omega,psi} by McDowell's classification.

nodes.name: z-weight decompositions
nodes.statement:
The centre $\mathfrak{z}$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{l}=\mathfrak{l}_\psi$ acts semisimply on $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$.  Since $\mathfrak{z}\subseteq\mathfrak{h}$, it also acts semisimply on the induced module $M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\mathfrak{g})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ and on its simple quotient $L_{\Omega,\psi}$.  That is,
  $$M_{\Omega,\psi}=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak{z}^*}M_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\hbox{\ and\ }L_{\Omega,\psi}=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak{z}^*}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu,$$
  where $V^\mu=\{v\in V\ :\ hv=\mu(h)v\hbox{\ for all\ }h\in\mathfrak{z}\}$ for any $\mathfrak{g}$-module $V$.
nodes.statement_short: z acts semisimply, giving weight decompositions of M and L.

nodes.name: Weights bounded by Omega-bar
nodes.statement:
Since $\mathfrak{z}$ acts on $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ by the restriction $\overline{\Omega}$ of the character $\Omega$ to $\mathfrak{z}$, it acts on
  $$M_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}})\otimes_\mathbb{C}U(\mathfrak{p})\otimes_{U(\mathfrak{p})}Y_{\Omega,\psi}=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}})\otimes_\mathbb{C} Y_{\Omega,\psi}$$
  by weights bounded above by $\overline{\Omega}$.  Similarly, 
\begin{equation} L_{\Omega,\psi}=\bigoplus_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Weights of M and L are bounded above by the restriction of Omega.

nodes.name: Decompose a Whittaker vector
nodes.statement: Let $v$ be a Whittaker vector in $L_{\Omega,\psi}$, with decomposition $v=\sum_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}v_\mu$ relative to (\ref{star}).
nodes.statement_short: Write a Whittaker vector v as a sum of weight components.

nodes.name: Case x in l_+
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\mathfrak{n}=\mathfrak{l}_+\oplus\mathfrak{m}$ be a root vector in a root space $\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$.  If $x\in\mathfrak{l}_+$, then $\mathfrak{z}$ commutes with $x$ and $xL_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\subseteq L_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu$.  In particular, $\sum_\mu\psi(x)v_\mu=xv=\sum_\mu xv_\mu$, so by comparing graded components, $xv_\mu=\psi(x)v_\mu$ for all $\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: For root vectors in l_+, components are preserved, so each v_mu is an eigenvector.

nodes.name: Case x in m
nodes.statement:
If $x\in\mathfrak{m}$, then
$$zx=x(z+\alpha(z)),$$
for all $z\in\mathfrak{z}$, so
$$xL_{\Omega,\psi}^\mu\subseteq L_{\Omega,\psi}^{\mu+\overline{\alpha}},$$
where $\overline{\alpha}$ is the restriction of $\alpha$ to $\mathfrak{z}$.  But $\psi$ vanishes on $\mathfrak{m}$ by construction, so
$$0=xv=\sum_{\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}}xv_\mu.$$
Each $xv_\mu$ belongs to a distinct graded component, so $xv_\mu=0$ for all $\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: For root vectors in m, x shifts weights and psi vanishes, so x kills each v_mu.

nodes.name: Components are Whittaker vectors
nodes.statement: The subalgebras $\mathfrak{l}_+$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ are spanned by root vectors, so $xv_\mu=\psi(x)v_\mu$ for all $x\in\mathfrak{n}$ and $\mu\preceq\overline{\Omega}$.  That is, $v_\mu\in\hbox{Wh}\,V$ for all $\mu$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine cases: each component v_mu is a Whittaker vector.

nodes.name: Lower components vanish
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu\prec\overline{\Omega}$.  Then by degree considerations, the submodule
$$U(\mathfrak{g})v_\mu=U(\overline{\mathfrak{m}}\oplus\mathfrak{l})v_\mu\subseteq\sum_{\lambda\preceq\mu}L_{\Omega,\psi}^\lambda$$
is proper in $L_{\Omega,\psi}$.  As $L_{\Omega,\psi}$ is simple, we see that $v_\mu=0$ and $v=v_{\overline{\Omega}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower components generate proper submodules, so they vanish by simplicity.

nodes.name: Apply Kostant's criterion
nodes.statement: Therefore, $v$ is a Whittaker vector in the simple $\mathfrak{s}$-Whittaker module $Y_{\Omega,\psi}=L_{\Omega,\psi}^{\overline{\Omega}}$ of type $\overline{\psi}$, where $\overline{\psi}$ is the restriction of $\psi$ to the positive part $\mathfrak{l}_+$ of $\mathfrak{s}=[\mathfrak{l},\mathfrak{l}]$.  As $Y_{\Omega,\psi}$ is non-singular, Kostant's criterion \cite[Theorem 3.6.1]{kostant78} applies, and its space $W$ of Whittaker vectors is $1$-dimensional.
nodes.statement_short: v lies in the non-singular s-module Y_{Omega,psi}, whose Whittaker space is 1-dimensional by Kostant.

nodes.name: Wh L is one-dimensional
nodes.statement: The space $\hbox{Wh}\,L_{\Omega,\psi}\subseteq W$ is thus also $1$-dimensional.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude Wh L_{Omega,psi} is 1-dimensional.

nodes.name: Reduce to finite length; induction base
nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, we may assume that $M$ is of finite length and has a composition series
$$0=M_0\subset M_1\subset\cdots\subset M_\ell=M.$$
We induct on the length $\ell$ of $M$, and as the base case $\ell=0$ is trivial, we may assume that $\ell>0$.
nodes.statement_short: WLOG M has finite length; induct on the length, the base case being trivial.

nodes.name: Subquotients are Whittaker modules
nodes.statement: For any $i>0$ and nonzero $m\in M_i/M_{i-1}$, the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{n}$ acts on the finite dimensional space $U(\mathfrak{n})m$.  By Lie's theorem, $U(\mathfrak{n})m\subseteq M_i/M_{i-1}$ contains a nonzero Whittaker vector $n$, and by simplicity $M_i/M_{i-1}=U(\mathfrak{g})n$ is thus a Whittaker module.
nodes.statement_short: By Lie's theorem each composition factor contains a Whittaker vector, hence is a Whittaker module.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 3.2 to factors
nodes.statement: The space $\hbox{Wh}(M_i/M_{i-1})$ is $1$-dimensional by Theorem \ref{mainthm}.
nodes.statement_short: Each factor has 1-dimensional Whittaker space by Theorem 3.2.

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: If $v,w\in M$ are nonzero Whittaker vectors, then their images $v+M_{\ell-1}$ and $w+M_{\ell-1}$ lie in the $1$-dimensional space $\hbox{Wh}(M_\ell/M_{\ell-1})$. The vector $v$ is thus of the form $\lambda w + u$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ and $u\in M_{\ell-1}$.  As $u=v-\lambda w$ is clearly also a Whittaker vector and $\dim\hbox{Wh}(M_{\ell-1})\leq \ell-1$ by induction, it follows that $\dim\hbox{Wh}\,M\leq 1+\dim\hbox{Wh}(M_{\ell-1})\leq\ell.$
nodes.statement_short: Two Whittaker vectors differ modulo M_{l-1} by a scalar; induction gives dim Wh M <= l.
